turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Um, I came in today because I just can't seem to stop worrying. It feels like I'm worrying about everything all at once, and I can't turn it off. 

I'm constantly stressing over my marriage, whether my performance is slipping at work, the bills... even the house projects I keep starting and then dropping. It just all piles up, and I spend most of my time worrying that I'm basically failing as a husband and a father. It's just gotten to be too much.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient reports pervasive, persistent anxiety across multiple life domains including marriage, work, finances, and family roles.
symptom_reasoning.S057: The patient explicitly describes an inability to control the anxiety, stating they cannot stop worrying and cannot turn it off.

turns.doctor_question: When you're experiencing this worry, do you ever have sudden episodes where your heart races, you feel short of breath, or you get a sense of panic or dread that comes on quickly?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My heart doesn't race, and I can breathe fine. It's not really a sudden feeling that comes out of nowhere... it's just this constant, heavy stress that's always running in the background and never really stops.

turns.doctor_question: Did this constant worrying start around the time something specific happened in your life, or has it been a pattern for you for as long as you can remember?
turns.patient_response: Well, it hasn't been a lifelong thing, no. I'd say it really started getting bad about nine months ago. That was right around the time this big cloud migration project ramped up at work, and... well, it's also when the arguments at home started becoming a regular thing. So, yeah, it's been going on constantly for about nine months now.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient confirms that the constant worrying has been ongoing continuously for about nine months.

turns.doctor_question: When you worry about these different things—your marriage, work performance, bills, and the house projects—do you find that the worry tends to be mostly about one or two main things, or does it really jump around to many different topics throughout the day?
turns.patient_response: It definitely jumps around. Um, it's rarely just one or two things. I'll start out stressing about the migration project at work, and then... well, before I know it, I'm worrying about the mortgage, or something I didn't finish around the house, and then how my wife is going to react to that. It just bounces from one topic to the next, all day long.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient clearly describes persistent worry that jumps across multiple different topics and life domains (work, finances, chores, relationship) throughout the day.
